thread:
marie: Heads-up — starting Monarch-11B int4 bring-up on dedicated rack. Quick smoke shows a weird summarization quality regression vs fp16 baseline.
eduardo: thanks — can you paste a minimal repro? is this during sampling or the logits post-quant?
marie: early run on our test-suite (news-summary prompts) diverges: outputs shorter, more hallucinations. perplexity on validation set went +12%.
zach: did you use per-channel quant or symmetric per-tensor? int4 configs can be wild.
marie: per-channel with clipping (our usual). Also noticed tokenizer mapping for the separator token looks different after conversion.
anika: separator token mapping? hmm — did vocab get remapped during conversion pipeline (mmap+merge)?
marie: snippet:
```
# from tokenizer sanity check
tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<sep>", "<pad>", "<s>", "</s>"])
# -> [30001, 0, 1, 2]
# but model embeddings expect: [30002, 0, 1, 2]
```
marie: so one token id off for <sep>. model-vocab and tokenizer-vocab differ by 1 for a few sentinels.
eduardo: ah that would explain some prompt prefix misalignment. was a merge step applied? which exporter was used to build the int4 snapshot?
marie: used exporter v0.9.2 -> int4-fast branch. conversion log shows a warning but pipeline continued:
```
WARNING: remapped 3 ids due to overlap; using fallback offset 1
```
sam: can you grep the checkpoint for embedding-shift? I’ve seen exporters that append a sentinel and shift the tail.
zach: also check rotary params — Monarch uses headwise rotary_scale!=1. If tokenizer shift happened, kvcache indexing + rotary phase may mismatch and amplify errors.
anika: good call — if rotary_freq/headwise order is off we can get stable but wrong attention patterns. marie, can you dump first-layer rotary scale weights and token ids for first 8 tokens?
marie: attaching quick dump in artifact: gcs://redwood-onboard/monarch/1712500001/rotate-dump.txt (small). sample lines:
```
layer0.head0.rotary_scale: 1.0
layer0.head1.rotary_scale: 0.875
first_tokens_ids: [1, 101, 30001, 502]
```
ci-bot: CI artifact uploaded: gcs://redwood-onboard/monarch/1712500001/rotate-dump.txt :white_check_mark:
eduardo: thanks. another suspicious bit: KV cache mismatch messages during streaming tests:
```
KV cache length mismatch: expected 128, got 127 — dropping last token
```
eduardo: that off-by-one plus token id shift + headwise rotary != 1 is a plausible multiplier for the regression.
marie: confirmed: when I remap tokenizer to model vocab (apply -1 offset for those 3 sentinels) and rerun int4 eval, rouge scores bounce back to within -1% of fp16.
zach: that's a good narrow fix. but we should also patch the exporter to preserve sentinel ordering or emit a mapping file.
san: (cc @anika) do we have a standard place to record token-translation tables during conversion? otherwise future bring-ups will stumble.
anika: we have converters/mappings/ in the repo but exporters don't always populate them. filing an action: add explicit mapping json and a CI check that tokenizer ids align with embeddings post-conversion.
eduardo: on the int4 side — let's also re-run a quick quant-ablation: per-channel vs per-tensor and symmetric vs asymmetric scale. if mapping was the major hit, quant differences should be small.
marie: running per-tensor symmetric now on a 500-sample subset. if that also fails, we'll dive deeper into rotary head ordering.
sam: FYI I hit a weird case on an internal long-context eval: positional wrap-around + rotated-phase produced attention bleed at 8k window — might be unrelated but file as follow-up.
marie: thanks all. immediate plan:
- apply tokenizer->model id patch for the 3 sentinels and rerun full eval (marie)
- add exporter mapping json + CI assertion (anika)
- run quant ablation per-channel vs per-tensor (eduardo)
- triage rotary head-ordering if regression persists (zach)

marie: will post updated results in this thread when per-tensor run finishes. :coffee:
